newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 89 -3 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 143 -6 on last week
AMLC COMMENTARY: Cattle prices fell in most categories and in most markets for the second week in succession.

Price declines were particularly marked for the export cattle categories. Steers with Japan market specifications fell 10-15 c/kg in major Queensland, New South Wales and Victorian auction markets. Cows and steers suitable for the Korean market fell by similar amounts. In contrast, prices for young cattled suited tot he domestic market held firm or rose slightly.
Evidence of the soft export demand conditions can be found in the early closure of some processing plants in Queensland.
It is also possible that overseas beef importers and Australian exporters are acting cautiously in the light of some market uncertainties.
In the U.S., the cow run is underway. There are also major changes in this market occuring due to factors that fundamentally influence cattle prices.
December delivery corn futures are currently trading about US$2.60/bushel. This compares with a December delivery futures price of $US3.89/bushel in early July and $US3.15/bushel in late September.

Extra demand from U.S. feedlots for cattle, generated partly in response to the lower corn prices, is causing U.S. feeder cattle prices to rise. The rise in feeder cattle prices may attenuate the U.S. cow kill but there no real signs of this yet.

In Japan, uncertainty exists over whether beef demand will fully recover following the E.Coli problems. September beef imports were down 38 percent from a year ago. Responding to the uncertainties in Japan, the USMEF announced this week that it would pour an additional A$3 million promotional expenditure into this market with a television and print campaign due to commence in December. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
